newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr stuck in range by late Tokyo, eyes on US jobs.
newsitem.headline: Dlr stuck in range by late Tokyo, eyes on US jobs.

text.p: 0630 GMT TRADED HIGH/LOW AS OF 0600 GMT
The dollar was off its earlier lows against the yen by late afternoon Tokyo on Thursday, but remained stuck in a narrow range ahead of the release of U.S. employment data for June later on Thursday.
"Short-covering lifted the dollar/yen slightly in the afternoon as support at the 114.30 yen area proved to be firm," said a trader at a long-term bank.
Selling by interbank players and U.S. operators pushed the dollar lower versus the yen early in the morning, but the downside was limited by bids from Japanese trust banks near 114 yen, traders said.
Dollar/yen was lifted from lows in the afternoon on short-covering by interbank players, but the upside was capped by Japanese exporters' offers above 114.70 yen, traders said.
"There just wasn't any fresh incentive to push dollar/yen out of the 114.70 to 114.30 yen range in Tokyo today. People were on hold before the U.S. jobs data," said a city bank trader.
The U.S. employment data for June will be released at 1230 GMT.
Economists polled by Reuters forecast, on average, that non-farm payrolls rose 222,000 in June, after a 138,000 gain in May.
A larger-than-expected increase in payrolls is likely to boost the dollar but selling interest from Japanese exporters could prevent a significant rise above 115 yen, traders said.
"Exporters would probably be quite eager to sell dollars if dollar/yen rises above 115 yen after the jobs data," said a trader at another city bank.
Some traders said afternoon remarks by Bank of Japan governor Yasuo Matsushita were partly responsible for encouraging dollar/yen short-covering.
Matsushita said in a speech at a bankers' convention that the BOJ's monetary policy continues to aim at strengthening the basis for economic recovery.

Although Matsushita has repeatedly made similar remarks in the past, his reference to the monetary policy was interpreted as hinting Japan's current ultra-low interest rate policy will not be changed in the foreseeable future, a trader at another trust bank said.
Short-covering in mark/yen also gave indirect support to dollar/yen, but the German currency's upside against the yen was capped by Japanese exporters' offers, traders said.
Some exporters, falling behind the schedule in selling marks for the yen, have lowered their mark/yen offers to below 66 yen, traders said.
Mark/yen was at around 65.24/27 yen at 0730 GMT, after edging up to around 65.43 yen. It stood at around 65.24 yen in New York on late Wednesday.
The dollar was steady against the mark after edging lower earlier on profit-taking.
In New York, the dollar rose to another 40-month peak against the mark, closing at 1.7545/55 marks. The dollar closed at 114.45/55 yen in New York on Wednesday.
Dealers in Singapore said activity in the dollar versus other major currencies centred on position squaring ahead of the long July 4th weekend in the United States.
The market's focus was on sterling, especially the crosses such as sterling/yen which saw quite a bit of profit-taking, dealers said.
